## Compare training labels with model predictions

With the AI grader configured and enabled, open **Training examples** and select an example. The sidebar shows its original label and a separate **Model prediction**: Accepted (true) or Rejected (false), the model ID, and whether the prediction agrees with the label. Pending, disabled, missing-key and error states never count as rejection.

Only the visible, selected example is graded. The request uses the exact content-only Classifier input shown beneath its diff, including all operations in a multi-cell example. The label and provenance are excluded. Navigation cancels obsolete work; repeated inputs reuse a bounded in-memory cache for this view. Changing grader settings invalidates cached results. Errors are not automatically retried.

Predictions are advisory. They do not change source notebooks, review decisions, training labels or exported datasets. API charges may apply.

# Advisory AI predictions in Compare changes

Open **AI grader** (the sparkle icon in the left navigation). Enter your fine-tuned model ID, optional organization and project, and optionally a dedicated key. Without a dedicated key, Runme uses the OpenAI key in Authentication Settings, only if it is configured for https://api.openai.com/v1.

Enable automatic predictions and save to opt in. Opening **Compare changes** sends baseline notebook text and each cell's proposed content change to the OpenAI Responses API. API charges may apply. Comments, outputs, authors, review decisions and labels are excluded. Keys stay in this browser origin's unencrypted localStorage, never in notebook history or Google Drive. Only run trusted code.

A green accept button means the model predicts acceptance. A red X means it predicts rejection; clicking X still **undoes** the cell change. The alternative is subdued. Neutral buttons mean no prediction, disabled settings, a pending request or an error. Hover or keyboard-focus the controls for the accessible textual explanation. Colors indicate a binary prediction, not confidence. Human decisions never happen automatically.

Predictions use exactly the classifier prompt from trainingExamples.encodeSftExample, with content-only native operation payloads. Changes outside the graded cell remain at the selected baseline. Output/metadata-only changes abstain. Only completed responses containing exactly true or false are accepted.

At most two requests run concurrently. Leaving the comparison cancels pending work. Exact input/config matches are cached in memory for this mounted view; settings changes invalidate results. Errors do not trigger automatic retries. No prediction is stored as human feedback or used as a training label.

## Agent/API usage

The same functions are available through browser JavaScript and WebMCP. Configure non-secret fields with `suggestionGrader.setSettings({enabled, model, organization, project})`; enter secrets through Settings, not executable notebook source.

To explicitly grade a frozen cell transition, call `await suggestionGrader.grade({target: {uri: notebookUri}, comparison: {startRevisionId, endRevisionId}, cellId})`. It returns `{accepted, model, requestId}` without editing the notebook. Settings must be enabled first.

[Responses API reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/cli/resources/responses/methods/create)

## Grade as part of an update

Add `grade: true` to `notebooks.update({target, expectedRevision, operations})`. The existing default sends no requests. With grading enabled, Runme captures exact before/after content, persists the update, then returns advisory per-cell results in `updated.grading`. Settings must be enabled and configured. Each cell is graded independently against the baseline; unrelated head edits are excluded. Metadata/output-only updates send no requests. At most two requests run concurrently, without automatic retries.

`grading` contains `before` and `after` content-hash handles, `status` (`completed` or `error`), `cells`, and an optional `error`. Handles are not CRDT VersionRefs. Cell results contain either `status: 'graded'`, `accepted`, `model`, `requestId`, or `status: 'error'` and `error`.

A grading failure does not undo a saved edit. Never repeat an insert just because grading failed. If persistence fails, no prediction is requested; reread and reconcile before retrying. Mutation failures retain the normal partial-update error contract. If the calling execution times out after editing, reread the notebook rather than assuming rollback.

The template below requires an explicit notebook URI, cell ID and replacement source. No API key belongs in notebook source. Results are not stored as review decisions or training labels. For durable comparison/retry references, use `revisions.create` and the separate `suggestionGrader.grade` API.
